intro: Sepsis is the body's overwhelming, life-threatening response to an infection, and it can make someone very unwell very quickly.
points: Sepsis is a medical emergency — recognise it early and escalate at once, telling a senior or nurse, or calling 999.
Never wait to see how things go; the most dangerous thing you can do is watch and delay.
Say the word "sepsis" out loud when you escalate so others treat it as a possible emergency.
Watch for new confusion, fast breathing, very high or low temperature, mottled skin, and a sudden "just doesn't look right" change.
Your role is to recognise and escalate, not to diagnose or treat — you only need to be worried, not certain.
Stay with the person, keep them comfortable, note the time and what you saw, and support prevention through good hand hygiene.
